rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that the main process ends at a terminal outcome and that a later external event, such as feedback or a return, may lead to additional actions that are optional and are not stated as steps of the main sequence: Do not give such a later event its own start event with a chain running to a separate end event inside the main process. Model the optional follow-up as a separate process with its own start and end events, or as an event subprocess with triggeredByEvent=true inside the same process, with exactly one triggered start event and no sequence flows to or from it. Keep the main sequence ending at its terminal end event.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that the main process ends at a terminal outcome and that a later external event, such as feedback or a return, may lead to additional actions that are optional and are not stated as steps of the main sequence

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description opens by saying that the process starts when a participant performs a named action (for example identifying a need), so that action is a performed step that precedes the first described activity: Model a plain start event with no label that carries the action. Add a task named for the participant's action, placed after the start event and before the first described activity. Route the sequence flow start event, then action task, then the first activity. Do not put the action into the start event's label, and do not drop the action because the trigger already implies it.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the process begins through one of several alternative channels, and at least one of those channels is an action that a participant performs (work the participant does) rather than a distinct external occurrence

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the main sequence ends at a terminal outcome and that a later optional event, such as feedback or a return, may trigger further actions: Label the end event of the main sequence with the terminal outcome the description states for that sequence (for example, a completion or termination state), not with the later optional event or its follow-up action. Keep the optional follow-up out of the end event's label and model it separately, as the guideline on optional later events prescribes.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the main sequence ends at a terminal outcome and that a later optional event, such as feedback or a return, may trigger further actions

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a process begins through one of several alternative channels joined by 'or', so that each channel is a separate way to start the same case: Model a single start event followed by an exclusive gateway. Give that gateway one outgoing flow to a task for each alternative channel, and join the channel tasks with an exclusive merge gateway placed before the first common step. Do not attach the channel tasks directly to the start event or leave them unconnected to a decision.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a process begins through one of several alternative channels joined by 'or', so that each channel is a separate way to start the same case

rules_sent_back.instruction: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the main flow ends once a stated completion outcome is reached, and separately says that a later reaction by a party (such as feedback or a return) may lead to optional follow-up activities that are not part of the main steps

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that two or more activities are performed independently, by different teams or systems, and a later step can proceed only after all of them have finished: Model a parallel gateway that forks the flow before the independent activities and a parallel gateway that joins them before the first step that needs all of them, instead of a sequential chain or an exclusive gateway.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that two or more activities are performed independently, by different teams or systems, and a later step can proceed only after all of them have finished

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that a monitored step continues until a stated completion condition is met, and then names a separate result with which the process ends: Model the monitoring step as a task whose label keeps the stated completion condition, not only the bare action. Model the named result as its own task placed after that step and before the terminal end event, connected by sequence flows. Do not reduce the result to the label of the end event.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that a monitored step continues until a stated completion condition is met, and then names a separate result with which the process ends
